product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Doing system gain calibration
body: System gain calibration determines the body and T/R (transmit/receive) head recon scale factors that will achieve a known level of image intensity when you use the body and T/R head coils with a known phantom solution and protocol. The goal is that when the same solution or tissue is scanned in the standard body and T/R head coils with the same protocol, those tissues will have approximately the same image intensity level on a given system and between systems of like type.

product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: B0 Drift tool
body: If only a functional check is required, see Doing a B0 Drift functional check. If the functional check fails, see Running B0 Drift calibration. Unwanted changes in the main magnetic field strength can occur when the spatially uniform field component is altered for a short term, during the process of scanning, or when the spatially uniform field component is permanently altered. This is known as short-term B0 drift. All MR systems that use passive shimming have B0 drift.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > System

title: Doing DQA calibration with the Sphere With Spout (SWS) phantom
body: The 17cm Sphere with Spout (SWS phantom), replaces the DQA-III phantom for systems running MR31.0 and above. The Gradient Calibration Tool (GCT) offers the same functionality as the DQA tool for: Checking the gradient connections Checking the image orientation Calibrating the gradient and table related parameters (xfull, yfull, zfull and isoVectorZ) This tool uses the clinical head coil, a SWS phantom positioner, and the SWS phantom.

product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Calibrating LVShim
body: The LVShim tool is used to calibrate the system to achieve the field homogeneity for the magnet in actively shimmed systems, and does gradient shimming (as default for prescan) as well as test mode shimming (customer acceptance, system in-spec testing) on both actively and passively shimmed systems. The homogeneity of the magnetic field of the magnet is one of the fundamental requirements of the magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Calibrating High Order Eddy Current (HOEC)
body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.

title: Testing lead-to-lead with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

title: Testing lead-to-ground with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

body: When the MR Scanner is set up as a secure client through Transfer Layer Security (TLS), it can only send encrypted data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) to a server. The MR Scanner itself cannot receive any encrypted information from the server. Therefore, if the MR Scanner is set up as a client and either the customer or service personnel is trying to send data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) from the server to the MR Scanner, this transfer will not go through.

title: Background
body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.

title: Doing final health checks
body: Open a terminal window by clicking C Shell in the service browser. Type ping [internal address], where [internal address] is the IP address. For example, if your DICOM server IPv4 internal address is 192.168.1.10, enter the command as ping 192.168.1.10. Figure 1. Ping command Result A ping reply is received from the DICOM server. Navigate to the Image Browser window on the MR system. Select Tools > Network Configuration. Click Add.

title: Doing a backup of the configuration
body: In Cisco ASDM, navigate to Tools > Backup Configuration. Figure 1. Backup Configurations window Click Browse Local. In the Select File dialog, navigate to the folder where to save the backup. Enter the file name as CISCO_FP1010_BACKUP_MMDDYYYHHmm, where: MM = two-digit month DD = two-digit day YYYY = four-digit year HH = two-digit current time hours mm = two-digit current time minutes Example: For 3rd May 2022, 3:21 pm, set the file name as CISCO_FP1010_BACKUP_050320221521.

title: Configuring the OpenVPN firewall
body: UDP port 1194 is required for this configuration of OpenVPN. This port must be opened within the system network firewall. To open port 1194 on an MR Host computer: Open the Service Browser from the Service Desktop manager. Navigate to Utilities > Toolbox > Product Network Filter and click the Expert tab. Add a new filter with the following parameter settings: Name: openvpn Allowed IPS: * Allowed Port: 1194 Protocol: UDP Click Save in the Expert box.

title: VRE Reconfiguration
body: VRE is an acronym for volume recon engine, and ICN is an acronym for image compute mode. These terms are used interchangeably. VRE configuration copies the VRE operating system onto the host computer during first-time software loads onto new ICNs. VRE reconfiguration reinstalls the software onto the ICN. This procedure is needed after Replacing the Server Imaging Platform (SIP) (ICN Gen 8).

title: Description
body: The CD/DVD/USB interchange system is not considered part of the archive system but rather an ancillary storage device designed for sending selected images or an entire exam to referring physicians. When an exam/series/ image is burned to a CD-R or DVD-R or copied to a USB-Drive, the system does not consider the exam/series/or image as archived. Therefore, the archive column on the Browser does not change its state based on CD/DVD/USB interchange activity.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: CD and DVD Media Considerations
body: A recordable CD (CD-R) or DVD-R can only be recorded once. All image data that you want to record on a given CD-R or DVD-R must be selected beforehand, and will be recorded in a single pass. It is not possible to add data on a CD-R or DVD-R. When recording DICOM image data on a CD-R or DVD-R, you must always use a BLANK media. Once you have started recording, click [Quit] to close the interface. The system continues to burn data to the CD/DVD in the background.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: A recordable CD (CD-R) or DVD-R can only be recorded once.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: USB-Drive Media Considerations
body: USB flash drive can perform multiple read and write operations not as the CD/DVD. Before copying images to USB Drive, make sure you plug it into the USB port correctly and firmly. Your PC or laptop must support USB 2.0 specification and for data safety, use it in working environment: 0 ℃ ~45 ℃. Image data can also be recorded on USB-Drive in PDF or HTML format, using the Data Export function. USB flash drive has variable storage size.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: USB flash drive can perform multiple read and write operations not as the CD/DVD.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Saving Images to CD-R or DVD-R
body: Place a CD-R or DVD-R in the CD/DVD drive. Wait until the CD/DVD drive light turns off, which is an indication that the CD-R or DVD-R is spinning up to speed. Or, plug the USB Drive in the USB port and wait until the PC recognizes the disk. Click CD/DVD/USB from the Image Browser program list to display the CD/DVD/USB function program. The CD/DVD/USB function program can be sized by left-clicking and dragging the corners or sides of the window.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: Place a CD-R or DVD-R in the CD/DVD drive.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Restoring Images from CD-R or DVD-R
body: Load the CD-R or DVD-R into the media drive. Click CD/DVD from the Browser program list to display the CD/DVD Composer. Click Restore from the CD/DVD Composer. Highlight the data you want to restore. Click Local Disk from the CD/DVD Composer and Yes to the confirmation prompt. The only indication that the restoration is taking place is an hour glass shaped cursor. Click Stop to stop the restore process at any time while the system is restoring data.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: Load the CD-R or DVD-R into the media drive.

title: Coil prescription overview
body: Radio Frequency (RF) coils are composed of elements that can be used to receive a Magnetic Resonance (MR) signal. A "Coil Configuration" or "Coil Mode" is a set of one or more elements from one or more RF coils used together to receive an MR signal. Previously, each of these coil configurations were predefined as part of product development. These predefined coil configurations will be referred to as "static coil configurations".

body: Service manual mode receive element group selection For troubleshooting, it may sometimes be useful to acquire data using exactly the same elements used during a customer scan. body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Test sequence
body: Select PAC Related ICE BLD (software version 30 and later) from the PAC Diagnostics Test screen. Click Calculate Time for an estimate of the time it will take to run the selected diagnostics. product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Removing the Physiological Acquisition Wireless Station (PAWS)
body: Disconnect the Power/Signal (J2)and Fiber Optical cables (J1) from PAWS. Remove the four M6 screws securing the PAWS with the attached interface plate onto the SEP and remove the PAWS assembly. Figure 1. PAWS with interface plate (5917956) on magnet SEP Remove the PAWS from the SEP. Remove the four M5 x 8 mm Phillips flat head screws attaching the interface plate () to the PAWS (5717528-3 (Gen 1) or 5717528-130 (Gen 2)). Note Save the interface plate () for later use.
section: Replacements > Magnet Enclosure and Outer Electronics > Replacing the Physiological Wireless Station (PAWS)

PAWS with interface plate (5917956) Mount the PAWS with the attached interface plate using four M6 screws directly onto the Side Electronics Plate (SEP). Make sure the orientation is accurate, as shown in the image. Figure 2.

body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Installing the In-Room Display (IRD)
body: Put the new IRD on a padded surface to prevent damage to the touch screen and put the control panel cover over it. Figure 1. Control panel cover 1 Control panel cover 2 In-Room Display (IRD) 3 Pad Note Do not remove the screen's protective cover. Important Do not overtighten. Tighten until fingertight, then tighten one-quarter turn more. Secure the IRD to the control panel with seven M4 X 10 mm Hexagon Socket Head Cap Screws and seven M4 Stainless Steel Flat Washers.

body: System Power Off, under Access tab, is for customer use since it will require 1 hour at the most to power down the system to cool down gradient coil temperature, and reduce B0 drift in customer scan level. For service LOTO, use system shutdown for immediate shutdown. However, note that it will be required to wait 1 hour after restoring power for certain calibration and/or customer scan.

title: Removing the patient fan
body: Disconnect the power cable and ground cable. Figure 1. Cables on patient fan 1 Power Cable 2 Ground Cable Disconnect air hose from the patient fan by releasing the clamp. Loosen four captive screws then slide out the patient fan. CAUTION FERROUS MATERIAL HAZARD! Components in this procedure contain ferrous material. Ferrous materials can become dangerous projectiles within the magnetic field.

title: Cleaning the patient fan filter and patient blower air flow filter
body: If the patient fan filter cleaning is needed, move the patient fan assembly outside of the magnet room. Clean the patient fan filter then install back the patient fan assembly. Figure 1. Patient fan filter If the patient blower air flow filter cleaning is needed, clean the patientblower air flow filter outside of the magnet room. Figure 2. Patient blower air flow filter

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Installing the patient fan
body: Align the patient fan with base on the rear left hand lower cover. Slide the patient fan into the base. Fasten the four captive screws. CAUTION FERROUS MATERIAL HAZARD! Components in this procedure contain ferrous material. Ferrous materials can become dangerous projectiles within the magnetic field. Handle the components with care, and make sure they are secure at all times within the magnetic field. Figure 1. Captive screws Note Air hose length=3m is recommended.
section: Replacements > Magnet Enclosure and Outer Electronics > Cleaning or replacing the patient fan
anchor: Align the patient fan with base on the rear left hand lower cover.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. title: Power down the computer subsystems
body: System Power Off, under Access tab, is for customer use since it will require 1 hour at the most to power down the system to cool down gradient coil temperature, and reduce B0 drift in customer scan level. doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Removing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
body: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure. See Electrical Safety. Shut down and power off the host computer. See Shutting down/powering off the host computer. Apply ISC LOTO. See Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Open the ISC covers. Connect the Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) strap to the ESD bond point above the Direct Current Power Supply (DCPS) in the ISC and wear the ESD wrist band.
section: Replacements > Integrated System Cabinet (ISC) > ICE > Replacing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
anchor: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Installing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
body: Restore the ICE by reverse order. Notice Component damage risk Applying too much force when pins are not properly aligned to the corresponding socket will bend the pins and can break the connector or cable. J28 of the ICE front panel is a Twin BNC connector for the local oscillator (LO) cable. Align the pins and keys properly before connecting them. Note Restore the cables as shown below. J numbers need to be reconnected. Figure 1.
section: Replacements > Integrated System Cabinet (ISC) > ICE > Replacing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
anchor: Restore the ICE by reverse order.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Champion / SIGNA™ Winner 1.5T
title: Finalizing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE) replacement
body: Remove ISC LOTO. See Removing LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Start up the host computer/system. See Starting up the host computer. Run ICE Board Level Diagnostics to ensure proper functionality. See Doing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE) board level diagnostic. Do a TPS reset. See Doing a TPS reset. Do a check scan. See Doing a check scan.
section: Replacements > Integrated System Cabinet (ISC) > ICE > Replacing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
anchor: Remove ISC LOTO. See Removing LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC).

body: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure. See Electrical Safety. Apply LOTO to the ISC. See Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Remove the system cabinet rear cover (9 screws per each panel, and 6 screws to connect the two panels). Figure 1. Remove ISC rear cover Remove the ICN access cover by removing the screws from the system cabinet rear panel. Figure 2.

body: Insert the ICN into the cabinet and install it with two screws. Connect all cables connected to the ICN rear panel. Figure 2. ICN cable connections (Gen7 and Gen7-DL) Item Description 1 PCI-e cable to ICE J55 2 Ethernet cable to Hub Port 11 3 Ethernet cable to Hub Port 9 4 Power Cable to PDU Figure 3. PCIe cable connection - Dolphin 2 card Note Ethernet ports 1 and 3 are NOT used.

body: System Power Off, under Access tab, is for customer use since it will require 1 hour at the most to power down the system to cool down gradient coil temperature, and reduce B0 drift in customer scan level. title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. title: B0 Drift tool
body: If only a functional check is required, see Doing a B0 Drift functional check. If the functional check fails, see Running B0 Drift calibration. Unwanted changes in the main magnetic field strength can occur when the spatially uniform field component is altered for a short term, during the process of scanning, or when the spatially uniform field component is permanently altered. This is known as short-term B0 drift. All MR systems that use passive shimming have B0 drift.

title: ICN On/Off procedure for Dell R-620/630
body: This procedure documents the proper methods of shutdown for the Dell R-620/630 ICN. The ICN is powered up when the host is started. There is no need to switch the ICN on individually. If needed, you can switch on the ICN from the VRE Power Control utility. The ICN is powered down when the host software is shut down. To shut the ICN down individually, use the VRE Power Control utility.

title: Switch On ICN from VRE Power Control
body: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control. Click POWER ON ICN for the selected ICN. The ICN is automatically powered on. The Dell ICN displays the boot status on the LED readout, located on the front panel of the ICN. If the application software is down, you can power on the ICNs from the xterm command line. Type: /etc/init.d/poweron_vres start and press Enter.

body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.

Contact your sales person for information on available service license packages. Grafidy adjusts and compensates short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Use the grafidy procedure to complete eddy current compensation. Grafidy should be run in auto mode first.

title: Setting up grafidy hardware
body: Unfold the six-channel grafidy fixture and lock the arms into place (90° from the center plate). Note Make sure the six-channel Grafidy fixture is firmly pushed into the slit of foam support without any gap. Connect the Grafidy kit cable to the Grafidy kit T/R board and secure with screws. Put the fixture at the front (head end) of the table with the connection box toward the bore. Connect the Grafidy kit cable connector to the corresponding Local Tx port. Figure 1.

title: Running grafidy
body: Start the Grafidy tool. (For non-proprietary service tools) From the Common Service Desktop, select Calibration > Grafidy. Select Click here to start this tool. SeeRestore Start Values for Calibration. Do not zero out existing terms if the Start Values have been restored.

product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: Running eddy current compensation in Manual mode
body: Select the Manual Mode tab. Figure 1. Manual Mode tab Select the desired terms and click Scan. If the Prompt to Accept mode is active, a graph of the results shows after the scan is completed. If a good fit is shown (fit line aligned with data line), click Accept. The calibration values are saved to disk and used in the next scan. Repeat this process by setting desired terms for the next scan and select Scan. If a bad fit is shown, click Cancel.

body: Put any phantom in the bore and start a scan or do a check scan. See Doing a check scan. While the system is scanning, open the RF screen (scan) room door. title: Filling ICC primary water circuit
body: Make sure the facility water hoses are connected to the ICC. Close the three valves with the red handle (two valves for emergency cooling and one valve for filter flushing). Open the shut-off valve for incoming coolant on module FPU. Leave the shut-off valves (for outgoing coolant) closed. Open the valves for in and out lines of the cryogen compressor. Connect a transparent hose onto the emergency valve.

title: Running the fMRI Quality Assurance (QA) tool
body: The fMRI Quality Assurance (QA) tool measures, analyzes, plots, and reports data about long-term image temporal stability of the scanner in conformance with the fBIRN consortium. It also shows background noise, peak-to-peak stability, signal drift, mean ghost, mean ghost drift, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), signal-to-fluctuation-noise ratio (SFNR), and Weiskoff stability. Important The fMRI QA tool will only function when BrainWave is active.

title: Troubleshooting Arc Issues
body: Confirm BNC quarter-wave shorted stub filter cable of correct field strength is installed as shown in Figure 3 and Figure 4. Start with the normal configuration, keep all cables connected. Run a scan at TG=170. If there is no arcing after 15 minutes, end the test. Testing is completed. Proceed to Finalization. If arcing occurs, end the test and proceed with the following steps to determine where in the transmit chain arcing exists.

title: Finalization
body: Finalization Set the RF ENABLE switch on DTX1 to DISABLE (down) position. Confirm that all system cables are returned to the normal locations. Set the RF ENABLE switch on DTX1 to ENABLE (up) position. Perform and successfully complete a check scan. If the RF may have failed, proceed to the RFA procedure and run the body dummy loopback test and validate channel 1 or 2 performance. Otherwise, testing is completed.

title: Doing the Universal Power Monitor (UPM) functional check (Head and Body)
body: The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power chain. It compares the measured RF power from the UPM to the expected value stored in the UPM configuration file. If the two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the UPM stops scanning. The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the reflected power chain, using the same test as forward power.
section: Functional Checks > Radio Frequency (RF)
anchor: The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power chain.

title: Testing lead-to-lead with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

title: Testing lead-to-ground with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

body: Due to the increased security hardening of the SSH features, users who want to access the system remotely using SSH will now have to establish a secured connection using SSH keys. SSH allows for the secure access of a system remotely over a non-secure network. Remote access allows for remote execution of system services and direct access to the file system. Due to the nature of allowing remote execution and file system access, securing this method of access is important.

title: Product Network Filter (PNF) firewall
body: PNF is a Linux software firewall based on IP tables. PNF provides the capability to put a software firewall in front of the system. Filters may be configured to restrict which system services are allowed to be controlled by other devices trying to access the Operator console such as ssh, and which computers may access the system. This access is determined by configuring which IP addresses are allowed to access the system. DICOM access to the system can also be configured.

body: Certificates generated by the customer IT team for use on the MR system must comply with the following: Certificates can be self-signed or CA Authorized. The MR scanner only accepts certificate files with extension .pem. The following attributes within the certificate are mandatory: Common name (for example, server FQDN) Organization name Organizational unit name Locality name (city/locality) State or province name (state/province) Country name (country/region) Bit length.

title: MR Scanner set up as secure client
body: When the MR Scanner is set up as a secure client through Transfer Layer Security (TLS), it can only send encrypted data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) to a server. The MR Scanner itself cannot receive any encrypted information from the server. Therefore, if the MR Scanner is set up as a client and either the customer or service personnel is trying to send data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) from the server to the MR Scanner, this transfer will not go through.

body: Host certificates are the certificates provided by the customer IT team that allow for communication between the host and client. The keys that are used in the certificate management process are private keys and public keys. A private key is sent back to the host from the client, which is encrypted using the public key.

body: The keys that are used in the certificate management process are private keys and public keys. A public key is provided to clients who send a request to the host. A private key is sent back to the host from the client, which is encrypted using the public key. Third-party certificates are provided by a Certificate Authority (CA) to the host after a request by the IT professional.

title: Enterprise Audit Trail (EAT)-audit logging
body: Remote logging of system events is achieved using RFC 5424 or RFC 6587 Syslog protocol. The following sources direct log messages to syslog, which are sent out using the rsyslog service: User login, logout, and patient data transfer (EA3/EAT) Linux Auditing System (auditd) Linux operating system messages Antivirus start and end status Others (as configured) Note This instruction does not configure the remote (collector) system.
section: Software > Software Security > Setting custom security settings > Setting custom security settings > MR Cyber Security Manual > Importing and exporting Transfer Layer Security (TLS) certificates

title: Background
body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.

This ePO server should be set up by and maintained by an on-site IT administrator.

title: Service licensing
body: The SSA license is a softkey (software file) for GE HealthCare tools and information. This license is assigned to one specific system and can be downloaded by GE HealthCare customers or service providers. Multiple service license levels are available to manage access to different features, tools, and service methods. Contact your local GE HealthCare salesperson or service representative for more information.

title: Managing SSA service licenses
body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.

body: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control. Click POWER ON ICN for the selected ICN. The ICN is automatically powered on. The Dell ICN shows the boot status on the LED readout, located on the front panel of the ICN. If the application software is down, you can power on the ICNs from the xterm command line. Type: /etc/init.d/poweron_vres start and press Enter.

This procedure is needed after Replacing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen-5, 6, or 7.

title: Backup current rules
body: Use this feature for creating a backup of the firewall rules once the system has been fully installed, the options loaded, and the application features configured. body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.

title: Coherent noise tool kit
body: The coherent noise tool kit lets you isolate noise sources using a transmitter (Tx), receiver (Rx), and antennas. By putting the antennas in different locations inside and outside the scan room, you can measure the attenuation of the magnetic and electric field. This assesses the RF shielding's effectiveness to determine if there are any leaks causing coherent noise image artifacts.
section: Troubleshooting > Image Quality
anchor: The coherent noise tool kit lets you isolate noise sources using a transmitter (Tx), receiver (Rx), and antennas.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: Setting up the coherent noise tool kit
body: Put the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx) on the two tripods found in the tool kit. Notice Possible equipment damage Never turn on the transmitter (Tx) without an antenna connected. Connect the biconical antennas to the Rx and Tx units, using the male-to-male couplers. Notice Possible equipment damage Failure to connect the attenuators will result in receiver (Rx) equipment damage. If using the dipoles or rod antennas, a 10 dB attenuator must be connected.
section: Troubleshooting > Image Quality > Coherent noise tool kit

product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: Setting up for measurement
body: After zeroing the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx), select Meas, then Auto. Keep the Rx and Tx in their current positions and make sure that they are fully zeroed by selecting Now. Measuring should only take a couple of seconds to complete. Note When measurement is completed, the screen will show the message Scan Terminated Press 1-4 to save or Escape. To see the measured attenuation, click Esc. Select Show and then Last.

product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: Measuring with the coherent noise tool
body: DANGER Ferrous material hazard The tool kit contains small ferrous objects. The coherent noise tool kit receiver (Rx) tuned loop antenna with preamplifier contain ferrous material. Holding these units too close to the magnet bore will forcibly attract them to the magnet. To prevent possible bodily injury or material damage, these small ferrous objects should not be brought within the 200-gauss line of the scanner.

title: Using the software defined radio (SDR) tool
body: The software defined radio (SDR) tool is used to differentiate an external noise source from an internal noise source. Note Training is required before using the coherent noise tool kit for advanced troubleshooting. The training can be On-the-Job (OJT) training with another engineer that is familiar with the tool, or taking the MR Advanced Service class at HCI.

title: Installing SEMS software
body: Locate the USB drive supplied with the coherent noise tool kit. Put the USB drive into a USB port on the PC to install the software. Download the SEMS software by clicking Chiave USB V2.2. Click setup_v.2.2. A window will open that asks Do you want to allow this app from an unknown publisher to make changes to your device?. Select Yes. Note Running SEMS software as an administrator may be necessary.

title: EPI Ghosting Checks
body: White Pixels What to do: Run Echo Planar Image (EPI) White Pixel in the Body Coil and make sure you have no white pixels with the Transient Detection Module (TDM) disabled. Why? White pixels during EPI Reference scan may cause failures in the linear and constant compensation, leading to artifacts in the final image. Swap Phase/Frequency What to do: Select the exact protocol that the customer is complaining about, except change the Phase/Frequency selection, and scan.

body: There are 18 test points on the equipment room side of the PHPS2. All test points are clearly marked with their voltages and description. See Front Panel Figure 1. Front Panel A 10-Amp circuit breaker designated “PHPS2 Power” with indicator light is located on the front panel of the PHPS2. title: Installing and replacing fiber optic devices
body: Fiber optic cables can easily be damaged if they are improperly handled during installation or during the replacement of connectors. Proper cleaning is required because microscopic contamination in the fiber connection will cause intermittent signals, due to degraded signal power, resulting in failure of the component or failure of the whole system.

title: Powering down the ICN from root level
body: Log into the application using the root login. In the xterm window, type: /etc/init.d/poweron_vres stop and press Enter. The ICN(s) should turn off after one minute. Result The Dell ICN is powered down if the green power LED located on the upper left side of the front of the ICN is not illuminated.

title: Replacing the dual drive RF amplifier
body: This document contains dual drive RF amplifier replacement procedure. This unit is in the Integrated System Cabinet (ISC) (shown below). The dual drive RF amplifier unit is about 152 kg (335 lb). The unit weighs enough that the use of a hoist kit is required. This document details the correct way to use a hoist kit to remove the dual drive RF amplifier unit and replace with the field replaceable unit (FRU) safely. Figure 1. Dual drive RF amplifier

body: Put the new battery in the socket on the Dell computer system board. Push the battery down until the release latch moves back into place and secures the battery. Connect the short ground lead that connects the left side panel to the Global Operator Cabinet (GOC) main chassis at the center of the lead. Secure the left side panel to the GOC.

body: Slide the DVD drive into the slot on the chassis. Tighten the screw to secure the DVD drive to the chassis. Install the side cover. Hold and align the bottom of the side cover to the chassis. body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. title: Removing the patient table dock
body: Remove the nut, washers, and clamp bracket from the anchor stud. If the site has followed the Pre-Installation Manual (PIM) and the anchor is a two-part assembly, remove the anchor stud (bolt) from the female sleeve anchor, use hand-force to turn the stud. This lets the dock stay flush with the floor during removal. This is the preferred method. Remove four sets of spherical washer sets, lock washers, and nuts, one set from each of the mounting studs. Figure 1.

body: System Power Off, under Access tab, is for customer use since it will require 1 hour at the most to power down the system to cool down gradient coil temperature, and reduce B0 drift in customer scan level. title: Removing the 1-piece bridge
body: Shut down and power off the host computer. See Shutting down the host computer. Apply LOTO to the ISC. See Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Undock the patient table and move it away from the magnet. On the service end, remove the UTNS antenna assembly and retain the parts for installation on the replacement bridge. Remove the nut securing the BNC adapter. Remove the washer from the BNC adapter. Remove the BNC adapter from the bracket. Figure 1.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

body: Make sure the nut portion of the caster pin is above the hook of the brake linkage plate. Adjust the caster to bring the nut above the hook if required. (For wireless gating) Establish communication between the PAT and the Physiological Acquisition Wireless Station (PAWS) by pressing the soft button on the PAT while in the scan room and waiting for the wireless signal strength LED to illuminate solid green.

title: Measuring the dockable table bosses
body: Download and open the Alignment Data Sheet Macro (DOC2647017) from the online documentation library. Notice Potential equipment damage The hook can become overstressed and bend, requiring replacement. Do not attempt to fully engage the dock pedal if the force needed is too strong. Notice Potential equipment damage The ODU connector pins may become bent, requiring table cable replacement. Do not electrically dock the table prior to the table being properly aligned.

title: Setting up the alignment lasers
body: Assemble both alignment lasers on tripods with the adjusters. Place the lasers at the front of the scan room, at least two feet from the handle end of the table with the lasers pointing down the bore of the magnet. Important The tripods are ferrous. Keep the tripods outside of the 200 G line. Turn on the first laser with horizontal and vertical beams. Note Make sure the lasers are unlocked.

title: Verifying the dockable table movement
body: The patient table can be operated in either the docked or undocked position. Undocked, it can be raised or lowered using the foot pedals at the rear of the table. In addition, floor locks are available for locking the wheels during patient transfer. While the patient table is docked to the magnet enclosure, the table cannot be driven up or down by either the dock pedals or the foot pedals at the rear of the table.

body: If the patient table is lowered, raise the table to its highest elevation with the Up foot pedal. title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.

title: Doing DQA calibration with the Sphere With Spout (SWS) phantom
body: The 17cm Sphere with Spout (SWS phantom), replaces the DQA-III phantom for systems running MR31.0 and above. The Gradient Calibration Tool (GCT) offers the same functionality as the DQA tool for: Checking the gradient connections Checking the image orientation Calibrating the gradient and table related parameters (xfull, yfull, zfull and isoVectorZ) This tool uses the clinical head coil, a SWS phantom positioner, and the SWS phantom.

title: Verifying the dockable table movement
body: The patient table can be operated in either the docked or undocked position. Undocked, it can be raised or lowered using the foot pedals at the rear of the table. In addition, floor locks are available for locking the wheels during patient transfer. While the patient table is docked to the magnet enclosure, the table cannot be driven up or down by either the dock pedals or the foot pedals at the rear of the table.

Leave 500 mm (align touch-and-go switch end and cradle top cover end). Note Figure 1. Egress handle Shut down the host computer. Refer to Shutting down the host computer. Turn off power to the ISC. Refer to Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Do the following steps:

title: Installing the string encoder
body: Find the label on string encoder replacement and record the manufacturer's position sensitivity number. This number will be entered into Guided Install as table encoder calibration value. Note If the PPI has 8 digits, round the last number to the nearest thousandth. For example, if the PPI number is 1000.7002, enter 1000700. If the PPI is 1000.7009, enter 1000701. Figure 1. Position sensitivity number (5772529) Figure 2.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Doing DQA calibration with the Sphere With Spout (SWS) phantom
body: The 17cm Sphere with Spout (SWS phantom), replaces the DQA-III phantom for systems running MR31.0 and above. The Gradient Calibration Tool (GCT) offers the same functionality as the DQA tool for: Checking the gradient connections Checking the image orientation Calibrating the gradient and table related parameters (xfull, yfull, zfull and isoVectorZ) This tool uses the clinical head coil, a SWS phantom positioner, and the SWS phantom.

title: Signal Scan
body: From the scan desktop, start a new scan by selecting Create New Worklist. Type geservice for Patient ID and 111 for Patient Weight in pounds. Click Show All Protocols to open the protocols window. Remove all other surface coils from the cradle. For flat (GEM) tables, place the curved adapter panel at the head end of the cradle. Place the split-top head coil on the patient table with the P connectors extending into the magnet. Lock the baseplate into the table slots.

product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: Noise Scan
body: A signal scan must be run before the noise scan because the same R1, R2, and TG values must be used for both the signal and noise scans. Do not run an Auto Prescan before the noise scan because the values will be changed. Copy the signal scan series. Right-click Signal Series and select Copy Series. Click Paste Series in the Rx Manager. On 3.0T systems, GE service personnel can use the Head SNR Noise protocol in the GE/Other protocol folder.

product_system: SIGNA™ Hero* / SIGNA™ Performer / SIGNA™ Pilot 3.0T (* SIGNA™ Hero includes SIGNA™ Hero XT, SIGNA™ Hero Elite, SIGNA™ Hero MAX)
title: SNR Image Analysis
body: Use a circular region of interest (ROI). Select ROI as 80% of the phantom image for the signal scan. For the noise scan, choose 100% of the rectangular ROI. ROIs in both signal and noise images can be measured directly in the image browser: Select MEASURE . Select the rectangular shape, and adjust its size and orientation so that the ROI is similar to the examples in Noise ROI Measurement and .Signal ROI Measurement.

title: Mechanical Hardware Check
body: Check the P connector for mechanical damage such as cracks. Inspect the contact pins in the P connector for damage from improper insertion or corrosion. Make sure the cradle latches and top latches are operating and have adequate range of motion. Confirm that the coil P-connector T-handle spindle is properly lubricated and not worn.

body: No Signal If unable to prescan, or scanning but receiving no signal: Check that the top half of the coil is latched properly to the bottom half of the coil. Confirm that the landmark is correct and the cradle did not unlatch. Verify that the scan locations and any FOV offsets are correct. Try scanning again. Note Be sure to remove the head coil from the magnet bore before scanning with the body coil.

title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.
section: Coils > Adaptive Image Receive (AIR) coils > Setting up air Posterior Array (PA)

title: Power down the computer subsystems

title: System Gain Calibration (for systems MP26 or earlier)
body: System gain calibration is performed to determine the body recon scale factors that will achieve a known level of image intensity when using the body coil with a known phantom solution and protocol. The goal is that when the same solution or tissue is scanned in either the standard body coil with the same protocol, those tissues will have approximately the same image intensity level on a given system and between systems of like type.

title: B0 Drift tool
body: If only a functional check is required, see Doing a B0 Drift functional check. If the functional check fails, see Running B0 Drift calibration. Unwanted changes in the main magnetic field strength can occur when the spatially uniform field component is altered for a short term, during the process of scanning, or when the spatially uniform field component is permanently altered. This is known as short-term B0 drift. All MR systems that use passive shimming have B0 drift.

body: The Echo Planar Test (EPT) combines the functionality of the EPI white pixel, B0 dither calibration and group delay calibration into a single tool with a simple user interface. The output is suitable for remote support access, trending, and automatic checking of results against acceptance limits. EPT automatically updates the Echo Planar Image (EPI) calibration files.

body: The LVShim tool is used to calibrate the system to achieve the field homogeneity for the magnet in actively shimmed systems, and does gradient shimming (as default for prescan) as well as test mode shimming (customer acceptance, system in-spec testing) on both actively and passively shimmed systems. The homogeneity of the magnetic field of the magnet is one of the fundamental requirements of the magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Calibrating High Order Eddy Current (HOEC)
body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.

body: Overview Normalization correction normalizes PET data to account for differences in coincidence pair sensitivity among the scanner's line of response. 3D normalization is divided into two components: Geometry component Crystal sensitivity component The curvature of the detector, gaps between detector units, and gamma ray penetration into crystals create spatial non-uniformity in the actual data sampling of any given view angle.

title: PET 3D Well Counter Correction (WCC)
body: Well Counter Correction (WCC) is a cross-calibration to the site’s dose calibrator. WCC uses the flood-filled phantom (water- and FDG F18 radioisotope-filled phantom) to convert the image data from counts per pixel to activity concentration per pixel. Work with the hospital physicist to fill the FDG phantom. The same WCC factors are used for time of flight (TOF) and non-TOF iterative reconstruction.

title: Troubleshooting problems with PET 3D Well Counter Correction (WCC)
body: If the calculated Well Counter Correction (WCC) activity factor is outside of the 4.75 to 6.00 range, a warning message will appear. The WCC activity factor directly scales image activity units, including SUV. The Calibration errors would lead to incorrect image quantitation. Potential causes related to the calibration procedure include: Incorrect entry of activity or measurement times. Incorrect or missing post-injection activity measurement entry.

title: Passive Shimming for PET/MR System
body: Shimming is the process of measuring the magnet's field over a fixed volume, then calculating and installing passive (steel) shims to improve field homogeneity. Do on-site shimming to compensate for unequal distribution of room steel affecting field homogeneity. Additional shimming may be required following any significant environmental changes near the magnet. It is important to do shimming after the magnet is sited and ramped with the magnetic field stabilized.

product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: PET insert mechanical alignment and adjustment
body: Overview This procedure explains how to align the PET insert within the gradient coil. The PET insert must be aligned within the gradient coil along three axes (X, Y, and Z). Alignment is accurate along the X- and Y-axes when the gap that separates the PET insert and the gradient coil is 28 mm (+/- 1 mm) all the way around. Use the PET/MR centering tool to determine these measurements at three points that are spaced 120° apart on both the front and back of the PET insert.

anchor: Overview This procedure explains how to align the PET insert within the gradient coil.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: PET insert alignment
body: Measure the Y-axis distance at the front of the magnet, starting at 0°. Use the centering tool (28 mm marker) to measure the gap between the PET insert and the inner surface of the gradient coil. Repeat this measurement at 120° and 240° (X-Y-axes). title: Running the fMRI Quality Assurance (QA) tool
body: The fMRI Quality Assurance (QA) tool measures, analyzes, plots, and reports data about long-term image temporal stability of the scanner in conformance with the fBIRN consortium. It also shows background noise, peak-to-peak stability, signal drift, mean ghost, mean ghost drift, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), signal-to-fluctuation-noise ratio (SFNR), and Weiskoff stability. Important The fMRI QA tool will only function when BrainWave is active.

title: Block Busy Functional Test
body: Overview The block busy functional test looks for detectors that are either oversaturated with radio frequency (RF) or too busy to respond. These conditions affect PET image quality. The block busy functional test is a functional check and not a calibration. This test evaluates RF interference from the MR process with the PET detectors. MR RF interference affects image quality and is evident by singles drops and block busy events.

The system should meet the following specs: Mean coincidence change between MR on and MR off (as a percentage of MR off) will be less than 10%. title: Doing the Universal Power Monitor (UPM) functional check (Head and Body)
body: The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power chain. It compares the measured RF power from the UPM to the expected value stored in the UPM configuration file. If the two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the UPM stops scanning. The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the reflected power chain, using the same test as forward power.

body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

title: Product Network Filter (PNF) firewall
body: PNF is a Linux software firewall based on IP tables. PNF provides the capability to put a software firewall in front of the system. Filters may be configured to restrict which system services are allowed to be controlled by other devices trying to access the Operator console such as ssh, and which computers may access the system. This access is determined by configuring which IP addresses are allowed to access the system. DICOM access to the system can also be configured.

title: MR Scanner set up as secure client
body: When the MR Scanner is set up as a secure client through Transfer Layer Security (TLS), it can only send encrypted data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) to a server. The MR Scanner itself cannot receive any encrypted information from the server. Therefore, if the MR Scanner is set up as a client and either the customer or service personnel is trying to send data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) from the server to the MR Scanner, this transfer will not go through.

body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Service licensing
body: The SSA license is a softkey (software file) for GE HealthCare tools and information. This license is assigned to one specific system and can be downloaded by GE HealthCare customers or service providers. Multiple service license levels are available to manage access to different features, tools, and service methods. Contact your local GE HealthCare salesperson or service representative for more information.
section: Software > Software Installation
anchor: The SSA license is a softkey (software file) for GE HealthCare tools and information.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Managing SSA service licenses
body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.
section: Software > Software Installation > Service licensing
anchor: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system.

title: Image Compute Node (ICN) on/off procedure for Sun 4100, 4170, Dell R620, R630, R640 (Gen 7), and SIP (ICN Gen 8)
body: This procedure documents the proper methods of shutdown for the Sun 4100, 4170, Dell R620, R630, R640 (Gen 7), and SIP (ICN Gen 8) ICNs. The ICNs are powered up when the host is started. There is no need to switch the ICNs on individually. If needed, you can switch on the ICNs from the VRE Power Control utility (Switch on ICNs from VRE power control). The ICNs are powered down when the host software is shut down.
section: Software > System Software > System Startup and Shutdown

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Switch on ICNs from VRE power control
body: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control. Click POWER ON ICN for the selected ICN. The ICN is automatically powered on. The Sun 4170 and 4170M2 take 2 to 3 minutes before the lights on the front of the ICN return to a normal (non-blinking) state. Wait for all hard drive LEDs to turn on, and for all lights to stop blinking. The Dell ICN shows the boot status on the LED readout, located on the front panel of the ICN.
section: Software > System Software > System Startup and Shutdown > Image Compute Node (ICN) on/off procedure for Sun 4100, 4170, Dell R620, R630, R640 (Gen 7), and SIP (ICN Gen 8)

The MAC addresses are printed on a sticker on the front of the ICNs. Click POWER OFF ICN(x).

title: Dual drive theory
body: Overview The purpose of the dual drive feature is to improve image homogeneity. Dual drive technology reduces shading caused by dielectric affect when scanning areas of the body that are more elliptical or irregular in shape (rather than circular), such as the thigh, pelvis, abdomen, and breast. The dual drive controls the amplitude and phase relationships between the two separate drive points on the system PET insert and minimizes the dielectric effect.

For example, comparing a 1.5T clinical BRAVO T1-weighted sequence to a Silenz T1-weighted sequence, there is more than 25 dB less sound within the bore, making the sound of the scan barely audible over the ambient sound of the MR system (within 3 dBA of ambient sound with patient cooling turned on).

title: Doing the Universal Power Monitor (UPM) functional check (Head and Body)
body: The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power chain. It compares the measured RF power from the UPM to the expected value stored in the UPM configuration file. If the two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the UPM stops scanning. The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the reflected power chain, using the same test as forward power.

body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

body: Do the MR-PET image alignment (VQC) calibration each time the PET/MR insert is removed or any mechanical alignment is done. This procedure checks for the correct relationship between magnetic resonance (MR) and positron emission tomography (PET) imaging. It also generates offsets used by the applications software to optimize the fused images. The mechanical alignment verification procedure and software assumes the magnet, bridge, and table are correctly installed.

title: PET Normalization Correction Calibration
body: Overview Normalization correction normalizes PET data to account for differences in coincidence pair sensitivity among the scanner's line of response. 3D normalization is divided into two components: Geometry component Crystal sensitivity component The curvature of the detector, gaps between detector units, and gamma ray penetration into crystals create spatial non-uniformity in the actual data sampling of any given view angle.

title: PET 3D Well Counter Correction (WCC)
body: Well Counter Correction (WCC) is a cross-calibration to the site’s dose calibrator. WCC uses the flood-filled phantom (water- and FDG F18 radioisotope-filled phantom) to convert the image data from counts per pixel to activity concentration per pixel. Work with the hospital physicist to fill the FDG phantom. The same WCC factors are used for time of flight (TOF) and non-TOF iterative reconstruction.

body: Look at the battery replacement label on the PET workstation to see if the battery should be replaced. The label is on the lower left or right side of the PET workstation. Replace the battery every 2 years. If the date on the battery replacement label is less than 12 months after the current date, order a battery. Replace it during the next Planned Maintenance (PM). If the PET workstation does not have a label (5661793), order a battery. Replace it during the next PM.

title: Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) Tool
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The tool does not rely on region of interest (ROI) placement as other SNR tools have in the past.

title: ACR accreditation scan troubleshooting
body: MR ACR accreditation is offered by the American College of Radiology (ACR). The intent of the program is to have a baseline quality standard for all MR diagnostic imaging devices. Accreditation is becoming more important as more and more health care insurance providers are requiring some form of accreditation as a prerequisite to procedure reimbursements. Scanners are assigned accreditation on an individual basis.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: ACR phantom scanning
body: Most failures in ACR phantom image analysis come from improper phantom positioning and errors in landmarking and/or slice locations. It is critical to properly align the ACR phantom before doing the ACR scans so the slice locations are properly placed on the internal phantom structures. Taking time to properly position the phantom reduces the time needed to complete these procedures.

title: Coherent noise tool kit
body: The coherent noise tool kit lets you isolate noise sources using a transmitter (Tx), receiver (Rx), and antennas. By putting the antennas in different locations inside and outside the scan room, you can measure the attenuation of the magnetic and electric field. This assesses the RF shielding's effectiveness to determine if there are any leaks causing coherent noise image artifacts.
section: Troubleshooting > Image Quality

product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Setting up the coherent noise tool kit
body: Put the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx) on the two tripods found in the tool kit. Notice Possible equipment damage Never turn on the transmitter (Tx) without an antenna connected. Connect the biconical antennas to the Rx and Tx units, using the male-to-male couplers. Notice Possible equipment damage Failure to connect the attenuators will result in receiver (Rx) equipment damage. If using the dipoles or rod antennas, a 10 dB attenuator must be connected.

title: Measuring with the coherent noise tool
body: DANGER Ferrous material hazard The tool kit contains small ferrous objects. The coherent noise tool kit receiver (Rx) tuned loop antenna with preamplifier contain ferrous material. Holding these units too close to the magnet bore will forcibly attract them to the magnet. To prevent possible bodily injury or material damage, these small ferrous objects should not be brought within the 200-gauss line of the scanner.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Overview
body: This procedure describes how to drain the individual Field Replaceable Units (FRUs) and cabinets containing coolant. These FRUs and cabinets need to be drained when completing certain replacement procedures. The FRUs are located in the Heat Exchanger Cabinet (HEC) and the Power Gradient RF (PGR) Cabinet. Failing to drain the FRU prior to return can irreparably damage it if the residual internal coolant freezes during transit.

title: Draining coolant from the XRFD, XPS, and XGA components
body: Put the open end of the drain hose into the pail. Connect the other end of the drain hose to the quick disconnect on one of the components (XRFD, XPS or XGA). Connect the manual hand pump to the other component quick disconnect. Pump the manual pump to remove the coolant. Use the funnel to pour the coolant into the flask and measure the amount of coolant removed.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Draining coolant from the XRFD PS component (MR750 only)
body: Hook the pump up to the supply side of the XRFD PS and the drain hose to the return side. No adaptors are needed. Place the open end of the drain hose into the pail. Pump the manual pump to remove the coolant levels specified in Table 1 in Draining coolant from the XRFD, XPS, and XGA components. Use the funnel to pour the coolant into the flask and measure the amount of coolant removed. The XRFD PS requires 130 ml of coolant removed.

The hoist consists of a service tool and system components. The winch with chains and spreader bar for lifting the replacement FRUs are in the hoist service kit. title: Removing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE)
body: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure. See Electrical Safety. Notice Risk of ICN damage The ICNs have software running on disk drives that can be corrupted if not shut down properly. Failure to properly power down an ICN can also result in premature ICN failure. NEVER use the power button on the front to turn an ICN ON/OFF. Follow the procedure referenced below for removing power to the ICN chassis.

body: This procedure documents the proper methods of shutdown for the Sun 4100, 4170, Dell R620, R630, R640 (Gen 7), and SIP (ICN Gen 8) ICNs. The ICNs are powered up when the host is started. There is no need to switch the ICNs on individually. If needed, you can switch on the ICNs from the VRE Power Control utility (Switch on ICNs from VRE power control). The ICNs are powered down when the host software is shut down.

title: Switch on ICNs from VRE power control
body: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control. Click POWER ON ICN for the selected ICN. The ICN is automatically powered on. The Sun 4170 and 4170M2 take 2 to 3 minutes before the lights on the front of the ICN return to a normal (non-blinking) state. Wait for all hard drive LEDs to turn on, and for all lights to stop blinking. The Dell ICN shows the boot status on the LED readout, located on the front panel of the ICN.

body: Move the FRU PDU/PGR cabinet into the place of the old cabinet. Unfasten screws for each angle shipping bracket and remove bracket from each side of cabinet. Follow Step 2 through Step 7 (above) to remove the cabinet from the pallet. title: Finalization
body: Make sure all previously closed coolant valves are now open. Turn on the PPMP CB at the HEC. Start the pump by pressing ▲+F3 simultaneously. Air will push through the HEC reservoir as coolant fills the modules in the PGR cabinet. Add the required amount of coolant to the PE tank in the HEC to get the level about 3 to 5 inches from the top of the tank.

Remove the four screws securing the driver module to the PEN cabinet frame. Figure 1. Driver Module - Rear Loosen the 16 thumbs screws securing the penetration panel to the magnet room wall. body: Attach both slide rails to the new driver module. See Slide Rails, Release Tabs. Attach both lifting brackets to the new driver module. See Attach Lifting Brackets. Attach the lifting bar (hoist kit) to the lifting brackets; attach the lifting bar to the hoist chain. See Lifting Bar - Hoist Kit. Ratchet the winch to tighten the hoist chain and begin lifting the module. Slide out the PEN cabinet slide rails a short distance to see how high to lift the module.

anchor: Attach both slide rails to the new driver module.

The HDDs are configured for RAID 1 with one each (master and slave) assigned for petRDFS and petLists patient scan data storage. A single HDD failure will not cause a hard failure of the PARC computer, but requires replacement of the HDD.

body: This procedure is only applicable to MP24 (Z820 PARC). This procedure provides instructions to control the synchronization (sync) of petRDFS or petLists patient scan data volumes when: Transferring a Hard Disk Drive (HDD) to a new PARC computer Replacing a failed HDD in a PARC computer
section: Replacements > System > PET Cabinet
anchor: This procedure is only applicable to MP24 (Z820 PARC).

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Transferring working HDDs to the new PARC
body: If the PARC computer fails or needs to be replaced, scan data on the original computer can be preserved by transferring the HDDs to the new PARC. Each of the RAID scan data volumes (petRDFS or petLists) are comprised of two drives. After replacing the PARC computer and transferring the HDDs from the original computer, the system will begin sync if necessary.
section: Replacements > System > PET Cabinet > Synchronization of a transferred or replaced HDD in PARC (MP24)
anchor: If the PARC computer fails or needs to be replaced, scan data on the original computer can be preserved by transferring the HDDs to the new PARC.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Replacing HDDs in the PARC
body: Each of the scan storage volumes (petRDFS and petLists) are configured as a mirrored pair of HDDs. When the HDD is replaced, sync will begin automatically and take about 6 hours. The System Readiness Monitor (SRM) turns red for petLists or yellow for petRDFS during this process. Full acquisition performance will not be available for petLists even though scanning can be done. The CSD PARC3 RAID Utilities provides the Stop Resync option.
section: Replacements > System > PET Cabinet > Synchronization of a transferred or replaced HDD in PARC (MP24)
anchor: Each of the scan storage volumes (petRDFS and petLists) are configured as a mirrored pair of HDDs.

body: Finalization The SRM will be red or yellow during sync. Make sure the System Readiness Monitor turns green, indicating sync is completed. Do a PET Daily Quality Assurance (DQA) check to make sure of system operation.
section: Replacements > System > PET Cabinet > Synchronization of a transferred or replaced HDD in PARC (MP24)
anchor: Finalization The SRM will be red or yellow during sync.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Finalization
body: Remove LOTO from the GOC power distribution supply. See Removing LOTO - Global Operator Cabinet (GOC) and Operator Workspace. Turn the host and PC circuit breakers on the PDU back to the On position. Start the host computer by pressing the On button, and log in. Note It is possible that the customer changed the default password. If you cannot log in, contact the customer for the correct password.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station
body: The charging cradle supports the docking and charging of the PAT. It is intended for installing outside the magnet room, typically in the control room. The charging cradle can be put on a clean, level tabletop or mounted on the wall. Note Make sure of the mounting method and location of the charging station with the customer before installing. Some sites may require their own facilities or contractor to drill and/or install the wall-mounted charging station.
section: Replacements > System > Operator Workspace > Replacing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station
anchor: The charging cradle supports the docking and charging of the PAT.

product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station on a wall
body: Slide the wall mount support into the back of the charging cradle. Make sure the holes align with the charging cradle as shown. Figure 1. Charging cradle slide onto wall mount Route the AC power supply cable at the back of the mounting bracket and secure using the supplied zip tie. Note The charging cradle has an IEC 60320 C8 receptacle for AC power. Starting in August 2025, charging stations are supplied with four AC power cords.
section: Replacements > System > Operator Workspace > Replacing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station > Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station

body: Attach the non-skid base to the charging cradle using two M3 x 10 mm pan head screws. Figure 1. Non-skid base screws Connect one end of the power supply cable to the bottom of the charging cradle, and the other end to a wall socket. Mount the two PATs on the charging cradle to start charging. Note The charging cradle has an IEC 60320 C8 receptacle for AC power. Starting in August 2025, charging stations are supplied with four AC power cords.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

body: The gradient filter attaches to the secondary pen wall (SPW) from the equipment room. The thumbscrews on the filter attach to PEM nuts on the SPW.
