anchor: The gradient filter attaches to the secondary pen wall (SPW) from the equipment room.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Removing the GEN1 gradient filter
body: Do LOTO on the PGR cabinet. See Applying LOTO - PGR Power Distribution Unit (PDU)/Gradient Subsystem. From the scan room side of the gradient filter, remove the plastic gradient filter terminal covers. Figure 1. GEN1 gradient filter assembly Note Two wrench technique: Use two wrenches when removing the cables from the gradient input/output connectors on each side of the SPW. One wrench prevents the post from turning, while the other loosens the nut.
section: Replacements > Gradient > Replacing the gradient filter
anchor: Do LOTO on the PGR cabinet.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Installing the GEN1 gradient filter
body: Lift the gradient filter onto the guide pins on the SPW and tighten the thumbscrews. When done, use a screwdriver to tighten. Attach the cables to the gradient filter connections on both sides of the filter. Start with the GND, Z-axis, Y-axis, and X-axis cables and ground wires. Snugly tighten each cap nut to attach the correct axis cable to the correct gradient filter connection. The lug connections between axes and polarities should not be touching. Figure 3.
section: Replacements > Gradient > Replacing the gradient filter
anchor: Lift the gradient filter onto the guide pins on the SPW and tighten the thumbscrews.

Ensure that both PVC valves in the coolant supply and return lines at the XRMw service end are turned off, and coolant has been purged from the XRMw coil. body: Do LOTO on the RF amplifier and PEN cabinet. Refer to the MR Service Safety Manual (5452735). The PAC is behind the left side middle cover. Figure 1. PAC location Disconnect all cables from the I/O panel except the white PPG cable, which is permanently attached. Remove the left side covers to access the PAC. Attach all previously removed cables to the replacement PAC. Replace all previously removed covers and enclosure trim panels. Check the alignment of the PAC with the enclosure in all three planes. There are adjustment screws that allow for adjustment up/down, left/right, and in/out.

Make sure the microphone cable from SRI (J21, J32) is not to close or touching the DS-DPP power cable (J7) or the DS-DPP itself.

body: While carrying the module into the magnet room, stay as far away from the magnet as possible. CAUTION Strong magnetic field! The module has no ferrous material and is not attracted to the magnet, but eddy currents set up by the strong magnetic field interacting with the TDM can make it very hard for one person to handle. When removing and or replacing the TDM on the side of the magnet, keep the module as far away from the magnet as possible at all times.

title: Replacing the cradle guide rail
body: This procedure describes how to replace the cradle guide rail. The cradle is locked in the home position with a latch on the patient table bridge. The latch engages a notch on the cradle guide rail at the rear of the table. The latch on the cradle should engage this notch just enough (without extra force) so when the cradle is pushed to the home position, it tightly engages the notch to prevent the table top from moving when the patient table is undocked.

Carefully turn the dock cover right side up. Reconnect the dock switch connector. Replace the dock cover on the dock base, and secure it with the four bolts removed earlier. Return the dock to the Magnet Room, and reinstall it using the tape that marked the location of the dock when it was removed.

body: On each side of the patient table along the top edge, there are Touch and Go (TnG) strips that run the length of the table. A closer look at the TnG strips internally shows that each side is made up of three individual strips connected by jumpers. If one of the strips fails, replace only that specific strip. In other words, you do not have to replace the entire side. Be certain of which strip you are replacing because each one has a separate part number.

title: Signal Scan
body: From the scan desktop, start a new scan by selecting Create New Worklist. Type geservice for Patient ID and 111 for Patient Weight in pounds. Click Show All Protocols to open the protocols window. Remove all other surface coils from the cradle. For flat (GEM) tables, place the curved adapter panel at the head end of the cradle. Place the split-top head coil on the patient table with the P connectors extending into the magnet. Lock the baseplate into the table slots.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Noise Scan
body: A signal scan must be run before the noise scan because the same R1, R2, and TG values must be used for both the signal and noise scans. Do not run an Auto Prescan before the noise scan because the values will be changed. Copy the signal scan series. Right-click Signal Series and select Copy Series. Click Paste Series in the Rx Manager. On 3.0T systems, GE service personnel can use the Head SNR Noise protocol in the GE/Other protocol folder.

doc_title: SIGNA™ PETMR General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: SNR Image Analysis
body: Use a circular region of interest (ROI). Select ROI as 80% of the phantom image for the signal scan. For the noise scan, choose 100% of the rectangular ROI. ROIs in both signal and noise images can be measured directly in the image browser: Select MEASURE . Select the rectangular shape, and adjust its size and orientation so that the ROI is similar to the examples in Noise ROI Measurement and .Signal ROI Measurement.

product_system: SIGNA™ PETMR
title: Mechanical Hardware Check
body: Check the P connector for mechanical damage such as cracks. Inspect the contact pins in the P connector for damage from improper insertion or corrosion. Make sure the cradle latches and top latches are operating and have adequate range of motion. Confirm that the coil P-connector T-handle spindle is properly lubricated and not worn.

title: Troubleshooting
body: No Signal If unable to prescan, or scanning but receiving no signal: Check that the top half of the coil is latched properly to the bottom half of the coil. Confirm that the landmark is correct and the cradle did not unlatch. Verify that the scan locations and any FOV offsets are correct. Try scanning again. Note Be sure to remove the head coil from the magnet bore before scanning with the body coil.

title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.

title: Coil prescription overview
body: Radio Frequency (RF) coils are composed of elements that can be used to receive a Magnetic Resonance (MR) signal. A "Coil Configuration" or "Coil Mode" is a set of one or more elements from one or more RF coils used together to receive an MR signal. Previously, each of these coil configurations were predefined as part of product development. These predefined coil configurations will be referred to as "static coil configurations".

body: The 3.0T Multi-Nuclear Spectroscopy (MNS) Kit includes a broadband exciter, amplifier, cabling, T/R switch, transmit switch, upconverter, and service coil for 31P spectroscopy. The flat or GEM table is not compatible with the MNS option.

title: MNS exciter calibration
body: The nuclei that are calibrated by default are 13C and 31P. To guarantee a linear output from the MNS exciter at other frequencies, you can edit a config file to specify which other frequency or frequencies that the site needs calibrated. This config file controls which MNS frequencies are used when calibrating the transmit gain tables of the MNS exciter. To choose frequencies to calibrate, open the config file and change the value for the desired frequencies from 0 to 1.

body: System gain calibration is performed to determine the body recon scale factors that will achieve a known level of image intensity when using the body coil with a known phantom solution and protocol. title: B0 Drift tool
body: If only a functional check is required, see Doing a B0 Drift functional check. If the functional check fails, see Running B0 Drift calibration. Unwanted changes in the main magnetic field strength can occur when the spatially uniform field component is altered for a short term, during the process of scanning, or when the spatially uniform field component is permanently altered. This is known as short-term B0 drift. All MR systems that use passive shimming have B0 drift.

title: Doing DQA calibration with the Sphere With Spout (SWS) phantom
body: The 17cm Sphere with Spout (SWS phantom), replaces the DQA-III phantom for systems running MR31.0 and above. The Gradient Calibration Tool (GCT) offers the same functionality as the DQA tool for: Checking the gradient connections Checking the image orientation Calibrating the gradient and table related parameters (xfull, yfull, zfull and isoVectorZ) This tool uses the clinical head coil, a SWS phantom positioner, and the SWS phantom.

title: ICN On/Off procedure for Dell R-620/630
body: This procedure documents the proper methods of shutdown for the Dell R-620/630 ICN. The ICN is powered up when the host is started. There is no need to switch the ICN on individually. If needed, you can switch on the ICN from the VRE Power Control utility. The ICN is powered down when the host software is shut down. To shut the ICN down individually, use the VRE Power Control utility.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > System
anchor: This procedure documents the proper methods of shutdown for the Dell R-620/630 ICN.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Switch On ICN from VRE Power Control
body: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control. Click POWER ON ICN for the selected ICN. The ICN is automatically powered on. The Dell ICN displays the boot status on the LED readout, located on the front panel of the ICN. If the application software is down, you can power on the ICNs from the xterm command line. Type: /etc/init.d/poweron_vres start and press Enter.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > System > ICN On/Off procedure for Dell R-620/630
anchor: On the Common Service Desktop, go to Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control.

body: At the host computer, on the Service Browser, select Utilities > Toolbox > VRE > Power Control Figure 1. Power Control Note The number configuration should match the number of VREs. The illustration above shows images from a system with a Sun 4100 ICN. Systems with a R-620/630 ICN have only one ICN selection. Confirm the ICN numbers and their MAC addresses. The MAC addresses are printed on a sticker on the front of the ICN. Click POWER OFF ICN(x).

title: Power off ICNs manually
body: Notice If neither the browser nor the command line are accessible, the ICNs can be powered off manually. Try this method before powering off the GOC. This is the preferred method because it does not corrupt the files on the hard drive. Momentarily press the power button. (For Dell ICN, the green LED is also the power button.) title: Calibrating LVShim
body: The LVShim tool is used to calibrate the system to achieve the field homogeneity for the magnet in actively shimmed systems, and does gradient shimming (as default for prescan) as well as test mode shimming (customer acceptance, system in-spec testing) on both actively and passively shimmed systems. The homogeneity of the magnetic field of the magnet is one of the fundamental requirements of the magnetic resonance imaging.

title: Running LVShim: Gradient shim in Auto mode
body: In Auto mode, gradient currents are automatically calculated after you click Scan to fine-tune the homogeneity of the magnet. In this mode, the tool stops after the X, Y, and Z harmonics are within specification. In test mode, the image from the last scan is automatically reanalyzed. Note For software version 29.0 and later, gradwarp is no longer applied to images. LVShim images may look more elliptical.

title: Calibrating High Order Eddy Current (HOEC)
body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.

title: Doing the Universal Power Monitor (UPM) functional check (Head and Body)
body: The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power chain. It compares the measured RF power from the UPM to the expected value stored in the UPM configuration file. If the two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the UPM stops scanning. The UPM functional check runs a prescribed scan in the reflected power chain, using the same test as forward power.

title: Testing lead-to-lead with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

title: Testing lead-to-ground with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

title: Configure user accounts for Role Based access controls
body: The system login control features are in the component Enterprise Authentication Authorization Audit (EA3). EA3 manages authentication and authorization on GE Healthcare Products. It supports local authentication and can also authenticate against Enterprise directory servers (MSAD, LDAP, and so on) to do enterprise authentication. An authenticated user will be associated with roles through its group membership.

title: Configuring password controls
body: Open the EA3 Administration window. Click the Local Users tab. Enter 3 in the Max Logon Attempts Before Lock field. The allowable range is 0-231. Enter 999999999 (or less, if indicated) in the Lock Duration (Minutes) field. Enter 8 (or greater, if indicated) in the Minimum Password Length field. The allowable range is 8-14. Select the Advanced Password Rules checkbox. Click Apply Configuration.

title: Service licensing
body: The SSA license is a softkey (software file) for GE HealthCare tools and information. This license is assigned to one specific system and can be downloaded by GE HealthCare customers or service providers. Multiple service license levels are available to manage access to different features, tools, and service methods. Contact your local GE HealthCare salesperson or service representative for more information.
section: Software > Software Security

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Managing SSA service licenses
body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.

body: Due to the increased security hardening of the SSH features, users who want to access the system remotely using SSH will now have to establish a secured connection using SSH keys. SSH allows for the secure access of a system remotely over a non-secure network. Remote access allows for remote execution of system services and direct access to the file system. Due to the nature of allowing remote execution and file system access, securing this method of access is important.

title: Product Network Filter (PNF) firewall
body: PNF is a Linux software firewall based on IP tables. PNF provides the capability to put a software firewall in front of the system. Filters may be configured to restrict which system services are allowed to be controlled by other devices trying to access the Operator console such as ssh, and which computers may access the system. This access is determined by configuring which IP addresses are allowed to access the system. DICOM access to the system can also be configured.

title: MR Scanner set up as secure client
body: When the MR Scanner is set up as a secure client through Transfer Layer Security (TLS), it can only send encrypted data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) to a server. The MR Scanner itself cannot receive any encrypted information from the server. Therefore, if the MR Scanner is set up as a client and either the customer or service personnel is trying to send data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) from the server to the MR Scanner, this transfer will not go through.

title: Enterprise Audit Trail (EAT)-audit logging
body: Remote logging of system events is achieved using RFC 5424 or RFC 6587 Syslog protocol. The following sources direct log messages to syslog, which are sent out using the rsyslog service: User login, logout, and patient data transfer (EA3/EAT) Linux Auditing System (auditd) Linux operating system messages Antivirus start and end status Others (as configured) Note This instruction does not configure the remote (collector) system.
section: Software > Software Security > Setting custom security settings > Setting custom security settings > MR Cyber Security Manual > Importing and exporting Transfer Layer Security (TLS) certificates

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Background
body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.

body: The MR scanner does not come with antivirus software. Antivirus software is an optional feature of the MR scanner. The antivirus software option includes both McAfee VirusScan Enterprise for Linux (VSEL) and VirusScan Command Linux (VSCL). VSEL uses McAfee ePolicy Orchestrator (ePO) to schedule and automatically update the virus signature definition (DAT) files. VSCL is a manual process that requires an on-site IT administrator to update the DAT as needed.

title: MR Scanner set up as secure client
body: When the MR Scanner is set up as a secure client through Transfer Layer Security (TLS), it can only send encrypted data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) to a server. The MR Scanner itself cannot receive any encrypted information from the server. Therefore, if the MR Scanner is set up as a client and either the customer or service personnel is trying to send data (EAT, EA3, or DICOM as configured) from the server to the MR Scanner, this transfer will not go through.

title: Importing host certificates - private keys
body: Host certificates are the certificates provided by the customer IT team that allow for communication between the host and client. The keys that are used in the certificate management process are private keys and public keys. A private key is sent back to the host from the client, which is encrypted using the public key.

title: Importing third-party certificates - public keys
body: The keys that are used in the certificate management process are private keys and public keys. A public key is provided to clients who send a request to the host. A private key is sent back to the host from the client, which is encrypted using the public key. Third-party certificates are provided by a Certificate Authority (CA) to the host after a request by the IT professional.

title: Enterprise Audit Trail (EAT)-audit logging
body: Remote logging of system events is achieved using RFC 5424 or RFC 6587 Syslog protocol. The following sources direct log messages to syslog, which are sent out using the rsyslog service: User login, logout, and patient data transfer (EA3/EAT) Linux Auditing System (auditd) Linux operating system messages Antivirus start and end status Others (as configured) Note This instruction does not configure the remote (collector) system.
section: Software > Software Security > Importing and exporting Transfer Layer Security (TLS) certificates
anchor: Remote logging of system events is achieved using RFC 5424 or RFC 6587 Syslog protocol.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Background
body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.
section: Software > Software Security > Importing and exporting Transfer Layer Security (TLS) certificates > Enterprise Audit Trail (EAT)-audit logging

title: Managing SSA service licenses
body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.

title: VRE Reconfiguration
body: VRE is an acronym for volume recon engine, and ICN is an acronym for image compute mode. These terms are used interchangeably. VRE configuration copies the VRE operating system onto the host computer during first-time software loads onto new ICNs. VRE reconfiguration reinstalls the software onto the ICN. This procedure is needed after Replacing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen-5, 6, or 7.

body: To request a service license, you need the unique 16-digit service license ID, that is assigned to the system. This ID is needed to configure and activate a service license softkey. It is a unique ID, meaning each system has a different code. The system language must be decided before getting the service license ID. If the language is changed on the system, it will also change the 16-digit service license ID assigned to the system and cause the existing license to fail.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual

title: Coherent noise tool kit
body: The coherent noise tool kit lets you isolate noise sources using a transmitter (Tx), receiver (Rx), and antennas. By putting the antennas in different locations inside and outside the scan room, you can measure the attenuation of the magnetic and electric field. This assesses the RF shielding's effectiveness to determine if there are any leaks causing coherent noise image artifacts.
section: Troubleshooting > Image Quality
anchor: The coherent noise tool kit lets you isolate noise sources using a transmitter (Tx), receiver (Rx), and antennas.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Setting up the coherent noise tool kit
body: Put the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx) on the two tripods found in the tool kit. Notice Possible equipment damage Never turn on the transmitter (Tx) without an antenna connected. Connect the biconical antennas to the Rx and Tx units, using the male-to-male couplers. Notice Possible equipment damage Failure to connect the attenuators will result in receiver (Rx) equipment damage. If using the dipoles or rod antennas, a 10 dB attenuator must be connected.
section: Troubleshooting > Image Quality > Coherent noise tool kit

title: Setting up for measurement
body: After zeroing the receiver (Rx) and transmitter (Tx), select Meas, then Auto. Keep the Rx and Tx in their current positions and make sure that they are fully zeroed by selecting Now. Measuring should only take a couple of seconds to complete. Note When measurement is completed, the screen will show the message Scan Terminated Press 1-4 to save or Escape. To see the measured attenuation, click Esc. Select Show and then Last.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Measuring with the coherent noise tool
body: DANGER Ferrous material hazard The tool kit contains small ferrous objects. The coherent noise tool kit receiver (Rx) tuned loop antenna with preamplifier contain ferrous material. Holding these units too close to the magnet bore will forcibly attract them to the magnet. To prevent possible bodily injury or material damage, these small ferrous objects should not be brought within the 200-gauss line of the scanner.

title: EPI Ghosting Checks
body: White Pixels What to do: Run Echo Planar Image (EPI) White Pixel in the Body Coil and make sure you have no white pixels with the Transient Detection Module (TDM) disabled. Why? White pixels during EPI Reference scan may cause failures in the linear and constant compensation, leading to artifacts in the final image. Swap Phase/Frequency What to do: Select the exact protocol that the customer is complaining about, except change the Phase/Frequency selection, and scan.

title: Installing and replacing fiber optic devices
body: Fiber optic cables can easily be damaged if they are improperly handled during installation or during the replacement of connectors. Proper cleaning is required because microscopic contamination in the fiber connection will cause intermittent signals, due to degraded signal power, resulting in failure of the component or failure of the whole system.

body: Log into the application using the root login. In the xterm window, type: /etc/init.d/poweron_vres stop and press Enter. The ICN(s) should turn off after one minute. title: Flushing Procedure for RF Amp
body: Remove Convert Coupler (BPV353 to NS6D10008) from DVMR pump. Figure 9. Remove Convert Coupler Setup as following steps. Notice Use towel to absorb any leakage of the coolant. Do not spill the coolant over the leak sensor. Notice When connect/disconnect the hoses, connect/disconnect quickly to avoid the excessive spilling of coolant. Hold a towel in one hand below the hose connector and connect supply hose for RF Amp. Disconnect return hose of RF Amp .

Lift the keyboard to detach it from the Scan Control and Intercom Module (SCIM) base plate. The keyboard is attached with Velcro. Pull the cable and defective keyboard clear of the SCIM and set them aside. Put new Velcro strips on the top of the strips attached to the SCIM. Figure 1.

body: Check which PAT needs to be replaced. Note If possible, find out from the user which PAT to replace. If the user cannot confirm the PAT to replace, test all PATs on site. While inside the scan room, press the soft button on the PAT to establish connection. Note The new PAT should have enough charge to complete the tests. doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station
body: The charging cradle supports the docking and charging of the PAT. It is intended for installing outside the magnet room, typically in the control room. The charging cradle can be put on a clean, level tabletop or mounted on the wall. Note Make sure of the mounting method and location of the charging station with the customer before installing. Some sites may require their own facilities or contractor to drill and/or install the wall-mounted charging station.
section: Replacements > System > Operator Workspace > Replacing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station
anchor: The charging cradle supports the docking and charging of the PAT.

title: Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station on a wall
body: Slide the wall mount support into the back of the charging cradle. Make sure the holes align with the charging cradle as shown. Figure 1. Charging cradle slide onto wall mount Route the AC power supply cable at the back of the mounting bracket and secure using the supplied zip tie. Note The charging cradle has an IEC 60320 C8 receptacle for AC power. Starting in August 2025, charging stations are supplied with four AC power cords.
section: Replacements > System > Operator Workspace > Replacing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station > Installing the Physiological Acquisition Transceiver (PAT) charging station

body: Attach the non-skid base to the charging cradle using two M3 x 10 mm pan head screws. Figure 1. Non-skid base screws Connect one end of the power supply cable to the bottom of the charging cradle, and the other end to a wall socket. Mount the two PATs on the charging cradle to start charging. Note The charging cradle has an IEC 60320 C8 receptacle for AC power. Starting in August 2025, charging stations are supplied with four AC power cords.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Preparation before installing VRMw gradient coil
body: While wearing nitrile gloves, wipe the magnet bore using a clean towel and isopropyl alcohol. Examine the electrical connection terminals at the gradient coil service end. Inspect the copper terminal surface and the stud thread of the gradient terminals for gauges, surface damage, and any epoxy or threadlocker contamination. If necessary, clean with an abrasive pad and wipe with alcohol wipes.

body: This procedure describes the replacement or installation process of the VRMw cable busbar. There are two separate busbars; XZ busbar assembly and the Y busbar assembly. Typically, only one busbar will be replaced at one time. Figure 1. Y and XZ busbars

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Y busbar removal
body: Remove the cable clamp. Note DO NOT remove the clamps on the busbar leads. Figure 2. Cable clamps At the service end, remove the safety covers from the end of the Y busbar cable connections. Figure 3. Safety cover Notice When removing the nut and washer, use the nonmagnetic screwdriver as a guide not to drop off the nut in the magnet. Remove two M10 brass nuts and Nord-Lock washers that secure the busbar lugs to the coil.
section: Replacements > Coils > VRMw cable busbar replacement
anchor: Remove the cable clamp. Note DO NOT remove the clamps on the busbar leads.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Y busbar installation
body: Make sure the rubber bushings (smaller side faces out) are on each mounting stud. Make sure the coil-side mating surface is clean and void of epoxy. Figure 7. Rubber bushing Note Observe the following: Before installing the replacement busbar, inspect the surface that will connect the gradient coil and cables for oxidation. If the surface is oxidized, clean the surface. DO NOT remove the clamps on the busbar leads. DO NOT lift the busbar assembly by holding the leads.
section: Replacements > Coils > VRMw cable busbar replacement
anchor: Make sure the rubber bushings (smaller side faces out) are on each mounting stud.

body: Remove the cable clamps. Figure 17. Cable clamps At the service end, remove the two safety covers from the end of the X busbar and Z busbar cable connections. Figure 18. XZ busbar safety covers Notice When removing the nut and washer, use the nonmagnetic screwdriver as a guide not to drop off the nut in the magnet. Remove four M10 brass nuts and Nord-Lock washers that secure the busbar lugs to the gradient coil.
section: Replacements > Coils > VRMw cable busbar replacement
anchor: Remove the cable clamps. Figure 17.

Rubber bushing Note Observe the following: Before installing the replacement busbar, inspect the surface that will connect the gradient coil and cables for oxidation. If the surface is oxidized, clean the surface. DO NOT remove the clamps on the busbar leads. DO NOT lift the busbar assembly by holding the leads.

title: Power down the computer subsystems
body: System Power Off, under Access tab, is for customer use since it will require 1 hour at the most to power down the system to cool down gradient coil temperature, and reduce B0 drift in customer scan level. For service LOTO, use system shutdown for immediate shutdown. However, note that it will be required to wait 1 hour after restoring power for certain calibration and/or customer scan.

title: Doing DQA calibration with the Sphere With Spout (SWS) phantom
body: The 17cm Sphere with Spout (SWS phantom), replaces the DQA-III phantom for systems running MR31.0 and above. The Gradient Calibration Tool (GCT) offers the same functionality as the DQA tool for: Checking the gradient connections Checking the image orientation Calibrating the gradient and table related parameters (xfull, yfull, zfull and isoVectorZ) This tool uses the clinical head coil, a SWS phantom positioner, and the SWS phantom.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Restoration

product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Finalization
body: Perform Table Functional Check. Perform the following Calibration / Functional check. Perform Coil Datapath Diag. Perform Dual drive quadrature tool. Note For MR31.0 and later, Dual drive quadrature tool has been retired, please perform Calibrating for quadrature. Perform ECG Leads Functional Check and Installation . Perform Peripheral Pulse Probe Check . Perform Pneumatic Patient Alert System Check . Perform Respiratory Gating Signal Checks. Perform check scan.
section: Replacements > Patient Table > Fixed Table > Cradle Replacement
anchor: Perform Table Functional Check.

title: Signal Scan
body: From the scan desktop, start a new scan by selecting Create New Worklist. Type geservice for Patient ID and 111 for Patient Weight in pounds. Click Show All Protocols to open the protocols window. Remove all other surface coils from the cradle. For flat (GEM) tables, place the curved adapter panel at the head end of the cradle. product_system: SIGNA™ Pioneer 3.0T
title: Noise Scan
body: A signal scan must be run before the noise scan because the same R1, R2, and TG values must be used for both the signal and noise scans. Do not run an Auto Prescan before the noise scan because the values will be changed. Copy the signal scan series. Right-click Signal Series and select Copy Series. Click Paste Series in the Rx Manager. On 3.0T systems, GE service personnel can use the Head SNR Noise protocol in the GE/Other protocol folder.

title: SNR Image Analysis
body: Use a circular region of interest (ROI). Select ROI as 80% of the phantom image for the signal scan. For the noise scan, choose 100% of the rectangular ROI. ROIs in both signal and noise images can be measured directly in the image browser: Select MEASURE . Select the rectangular shape, and adjust its size and orientation so that the ROI is similar to the examples in Noise ROI Measurement and .Signal ROI Measurement.

body: Check the P connector for mechanical damage such as cracks. Inspect the contact pins in the P connector for damage from improper insertion or corrosion. Make sure the cradle latches and top latches are operating and have adequate range of motion. Confirm that the coil P-connector T-handle spindle is properly lubricated and not worn.

body: The Gradshim process is done with a sampling diameter of 22 cm DSV and the same bandwidth as LVShim Fine, which depends on the quality (good/bad) of the fine tuning. When the scan passes and all harmonics are within specification, the magnetic field is reanalyzed in Test mode automatically at 45 DSV for customer acceptance. The Gradshim process includes LVShim - test. The objective of this test is to analyze completed scans at 45 DSV without calculating currents.

title: Doing system gain calibration
body: System gain calibration determines the body and T/R (transmit/receive) head recon scale factors that will achieve a known level of image intensity when you use the body and T/R head coils with a known phantom solution and protocol. The goal is that when the same solution or tissue is scanned in the standard body and T/R head coils with the same protocol, those tissues will have approximately the same image intensity level on a given system and between systems of like type.

title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.

The tool also has a built-in wait time to allow the phantom to settle before scanning. The Probe Tuning and SNR Check Tool is an essential part of conditioning a system for performing spectroscopy, to optimize both SNR and phasing.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Running eddy current compensation
body: Eddy currents are unwanted currents generated in the conducting structures near the gradient coils when gradient field changes which distort the ideal gradient waveform of MRI systems. The distorted gradient waveform creates many image quality problems, such as ghosting, banding, and geometrical distortions of the images. Eddy currents are generated according to Faraday’s law (part of the Maxwell equations), therefore it is a physical reality and can not be avoided.

title: Calibrating High Order Eddy Current (HOEC)
body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > Gradient

title: Doing power monitor function check (head and body)
body: The Power monitor functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power. It compares the measured RF power from the Power monitor to the expected value stored in the Power monitor configuration file. If two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the PM stops scanning.

title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.

title: Arc Flash Safety
body: Arc flash is a high-energy discharge of highly-conductive plasma, which can cause destruction to anything in its path. It is important to take the proper precautions when servicing energized equipment where voltage exceeds 50 volts. All unguarded equipment being serviced posing immediate exposure to voltages greater than 50 volts requires appropriate Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) be worn. Arc flash hazards are very complex and different than electrical shock hazards.

title: General Guidelines
body: Arc flash risks are recognized globally as a potential electrical hazard. Requirements and protective measures are guided by local regulatory requirements. In jurisdictions where PPE is specified, Hazard Class 1 or 2 PPE must be used. Arc flash may occur when de-energizing or re-energizing electrical equipment. Precautions must be taken during both actions. Comply with local regulatory requirements.

title: Background
body: From DICOM part 15, [RFC 5426] provides the mechanisms for rapid transport of audit messages. It is the standardized successor to the informative standard [RFC 3164], which is widely used in a variety of settings. RFC 3164 – BSD syslog protocol - This was the original protocol supported in EAT, and was Obsoleted by: 5424. This protocol has been used for the transmission of event notification messages across networks for many years.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: CD and DVD Media Considerations
body: A recordable CD (CD-R) or DVD-R can only be recorded once. All image data that you want to record on a given CD-R or DVD-R must be selected beforehand, and will be recorded in a single pass. It is not possible to add data on a CD-R or DVD-R. When recording DICOM image data on a CD-R or DVD-R, you must always use a BLANK media. Once you have started recording, click [Quit] to close the interface. The system continues to burn data to the CD/DVD in the background.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: A recordable CD (CD-R) or DVD-R can only be recorded once.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: USB-Drive Media Considerations
body: USB flash drive can perform multiple read and write operations not as the CD/DVD. Before copying images to USB Drive, make sure you plug it into the USB port correctly and firmly. Your PC or laptop must support USB 2.0 specification and for data safety, use it in working environment: 0 ℃ ~45 ℃. Image data can also be recorded on USB-Drive in PDF or HTML format, using the Data Export function. USB flash drive has variable storage size.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: USB flash drive can perform multiple read and write operations not as the CD/DVD.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Saving Images to CD-R or DVD-R
body: Place a CD-R or DVD-R in the CD/DVD drive. Wait until the CD/DVD drive light turns off, which is an indication that the CD-R or DVD-R is spinning up to speed. Or, plug the USB Drive in the USB port and wait until the PC recognizes the disk. Click CD/DVD/USB from the Image Browser program list to display the CD/DVD/USB function program. The CD/DVD/USB function program can be sized by left-clicking and dragging the corners or sides of the window.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: Place a CD-R or DVD-R in the CD/DVD drive.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Restoring Images from CD-R or DVD-R
body: Load the CD-R or DVD-R into the media drive. Click CD/DVD from the Browser program list to display the CD/DVD Composer. Click Restore from the CD/DVD Composer. Highlight the data you want to restore. Click Local Disk from the CD/DVD Composer and Yes to the confirmation prompt. The only indication that the restoration is taking place is an hour glass shaped cursor. Click Stop to stop the restore process at any time while the system is restoring data.
section: Software > Software Utilities > CD/DVD/USB Functions
anchor: Load the CD-R or DVD-R into the media drive.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Testing lead-to-lead with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.
section: Planned Maintenance > PM Procedures > Testing PAC leakage current > Using Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
anchor: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Testing lead-to-ground with the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.
section: Planned Maintenance > PM Procedures > Testing PAC leakage current > Using Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer
anchor: Select μA to start the leakage test.

title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

title: Draining coolant from chiller tank
body: Unscrew the cap from the chiller tank. Prepare draining tank and draining hose with L connector. Insert L connector to the tank draining nipple. The valve inside will open automatically by connecting the mating connector and draining will start. When the coolant fills Tank almost full (about 4 minutes), remove the L connector and replace the Tank. Then, connect the L connector to nipple to restart the draining. Wait until the draining stops from the hose.

body: This procedure describes the process to deionize and filter the coolant for the Gradient Coil (GC) loop and Power Electronics (PE) loop. The deionization kit will hook up to each of the cooling loops to increase the electrical resistivity level and to filter the coolant. Chemical additives will also be added back into each cooling loop. A general schematic of the setup for a cooling loop is shown below.

body: Unplug the deionization kit power cord and extension cord. Use the wrench tool to do the following steps. Remove the deionization kit housing and filter housing from the kit. Discard any residual fluid in the housings into a bucket. Note This fluid is bio-friendly and can be discarded down a normal sewage drain. Although the water is treated for bacteria and water corrosion, the levels of concentrate are safe for water and sewer systems disposal.

title: Doing power monitor function check (head and body)
body: The Power monitor functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power. It compares the measured RF power from the Power monitor to the expected value stored in the Power monitor configuration file. If two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the PM stops scanning.

title: ACR accreditation scan troubleshooting
body: MR ACR accreditation is offered by the American College of Radiology (ACR). The intent of the program is to have a baseline quality standard for all MR diagnostic imaging devices. Accreditation is becoming more important as more and more health care insurance providers are requiring some form of accreditation as a prerequisite to procedure reimbursements. Scanners are assigned accreditation on an individual basis.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: ACR phantom scanning
body: Most failures in ACR phantom image analysis come from improper phantom positioning and errors in landmarking and/or slice locations. It is critical to properly align the ACR phantom before doing the ACR scans so the slice locations are properly placed on the internal phantom structures. Taking time to properly position the phantom reduces the time needed to complete these procedures.

title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.

title: F-50H Emergency Backup Water Supply
body: Customer provided temporary backup water cooling is allowed for the Shield/Cryo Cooler Compressor Cabinet if chiller or ICC went fault and stopped running. The backup compressor cooling design can utilize open loop city water only as temporary backup during loss of the closed loop water from the 18KW Chiller or ICC. Long term running at open loop cooling systems will not allow a chemical equilibrium establishment and eventually contribute to failure.

title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.
section: Replacements > Magnet Enclosure and Outer Electronics > Replacing the magnet enclosure covers > Removing the magnet front cover

The application begins to shut down, which can take up to 15 minutes. When the shut down is completed, the screen goes blank and the computer turns off. Figure 2.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.

title: Adjusting cradle guide rail latch
body: The cradle is locked in home position on the Fixed Table by a latch in the cradle, which engages a notch in the cradle guide strip near the end of the Fixed table. The cradle should be able to just engage this notch, without extra force, when pushed to home position on the table top, yet it must engage it tight enough so the table top (cradle) will not move on the Patient table freely when it is not engaged with LPCA.

title: Cradle Guide Rail Latch Adjustment when Table is docked to Gantry

title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.
section: Replacements > Magnet Enclosure and Outer Electronics > Replacing the magnet enclosure covers > Removing the magnet right-hand rear cover
anchor: Make sure the host computer is shut down.

title: Shutting down the host computer

System Shutdown When prompted, click on the reason for the system shutdown: Daily, Service, or Other. Or click Cancel to exit the shutdown of your system. The application begins to shut down, which can take up to 15 minutes. When the shut down is completed, the screen goes blank and the computer turns off. Figure 2.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

title: Removing the patient fan

Loosen four captive screws then slide out the patient fan. CAUTION FERROUS MATERIAL HAZARD! Components in this procedure contain ferrous material. Ferrous materials can become dangerous projectiles within the magnetic field.

title: Installing the patient fan
body: Align the patient fan with base on the rear left hand lower cover. Slide the patient fan into the base. Fasten the four captive screws. CAUTION FERROUS MATERIAL HAZARD! Components in this procedure contain ferrous material. Ferrous materials can become dangerous projectiles within the magnetic field. Handle the components with care, and make sure they are secure at all times within the magnetic field. Figure 1. Captive screws Note Air hose length=3m is recommended.

System Shutdown When prompted, click on the reason for the system shutdown: Daily, Service, or Other. Or click Cancel to exit the shutdown of your system. The application begins to shut down, which can take up to 15 minutes. When the shut down is completed, the screen goes blank and the computer turns off. Figure 2.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.
section: Replacements > Magnet Enclosure and Outer Electronics > Replacing the GC Cooling Manifold > Installing the rear pedestal
anchor: Move cradle to end of rear bridge.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

title: Installing the magnet left-hand rear cover
body: Position the left-hand rear cover at the rear of the magnet. Install the left-hand rear cover onto the magnet. Secure the cover to the magnet by screws. Figure 1. Left-hand rear cover screws Item Description Part Number 1 M10 x 25 Socket Head Cap Screw 1000-M10C025-33 M10 Nylon Washer 2000-M10-30 2 M6 x 16 Socket Head Screw 1000-M6C016-33

title: Installing the magnet rear cable cover
body: Hang the bracket of the rear cable cover (8600600-442 or 8700700-442) on the hook of the T-shape bracket. Figure 1. Hanging the rear cable cover Install threeM10 x 25 Socket Head Cap Screws (1000-M10C025-33) securing the rear cable cover to the magnet enclosure. Figure 2. Securing the rear cable cover

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Installing the magnet rear trim ring
body: Align seven ball and catch strikers on the back of the rear trim ring with the seven ball and catch latches on the rear endbell. Figure 1. Rear trim ring alignment 1 Rear endbell ball catch latches 2 Rear trim ring ball catch strikers Install the left or right rear trim ring onto the magnet enclosure. Make sure the seven ball and catch latches retain the trim ring.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Installing the magnet rear service access panel
body: Lower the rear service access panel into position on the magnet enclosure. Make sure the tabs on the top of the panel engage the slots on the upper service access panel. Figure 1. Rear service access panel alignment 1 Tabs 2 Slots Slide the access panel forward. Secure the rear service access panel to the horizontal bracket with the screw. Figure 2. Securing the rear service access panel

title: Installing the magnet front service access panel
body: Lower the front service access panel (8600600-600) into position on the magnet enclosure. Make sure the tabs on the top of the panel engage the slots on the upper service access panel. Figure 1. Front service access panel alignment 1 Tabs 2 Slots Slide the access panel rearward. Install three M10 x 25 Socket Head Cap Screws securing the front service access panel to the rear service access panel.

anchor: Lower the front service access panel (8600600-600) into position on the magnet enclosure.

body: Align the five ball catch strikers on the back of the service access trim with the five latches on the front service access panel. Figure 1. Service access trim alignment 1 Ball catch strikers 2 Ball catch latches Install the service access trim onto the front service access panel. Make sure all five ball catch latches retain the panel.

title: Removing LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Alert necessary personnel that power is being restored. Remove the Lock and the Tag from the PDU MAIN INPUT circuit breaker. product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Removing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen 5, 6, or 7
body: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure. See Electrical Safety. Apply LOTO to the ISC. See Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC). Remove system cabinet left cover. Raise the handlebar on left cover. Figure 1. Removing system cabinet cover 1 Left cover 2 Right cover Unlock six fasteners with the coin. Remove left cover. Remove the rear cover by removing six screws from the magnet room. Figure 2.
section: Replacements > System Cabinet > ICN > Replacing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen-5, 6, or 7
anchor: Make sure that you have read and understood the electrical safety requirements before starting this procedure.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Installing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen-5, 6, or 7
body: Insert the ICN into the cabinet and install it with two screws. Connect all cables connected to the ICN rear panel. Figure 2. ICN cable connections (Gen7 and Gen7-DL) Item Description 1 PCI-e cable to ICE J51 2 Ethernet cable to Hub Port 11 3 Ethernet cable to Hub Port 9 4 Power Cable to PDU Figure 3. PCIe cable connection - Dolphin 2 card Note Ethernet ports 1 and 3 are NOT used.
section: Replacements > System Cabinet > ICN > Replacing the Image Compute Node (ICN) Gen-5, 6, or 7
anchor: Insert the ICN into the cabinet and install it with two screws.

title: Shutting down the host computer
body: Click the arrow on the Tools High Level Access tab and click System Shutdown or System Power Off (as applicable). Figure 1. System Shutdown When prompted, click on the reason for the system shutdown: Daily, Service, or Other. Or click Cancel to exit the shutdown of your system. The application begins to shut down, which can take up to 15 minutes. When the shut down is completed, the screen goes blank and the computer turns off. Figure 2.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.
section: Replacements > System Cabinet > DCPS > Replacing the Integrated Control Engine (ICE) DC power supply (DCPS)
anchor: Make sure the host computer is shut down.

PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.
section: Replacements > Patient Table > Replacing dock cover assembly
anchor: Make sure the host computer is shut down.

body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. Because logging on as a super user allows you to make changes that can do irreparable damage to the system, do not log on as root unless necessary. Note During some startups or restarts, the system may seem to have stalled. The system startup process can take an extended period of time.

title: Applying LOTO - Integrated System Cabinet (ISC)
body: Make sure the host computer is shut down. At the front panel of the PDU, press the Power Off button. Figure 1. PDU front panel Rotate the larger main breaker labeled MAIN INPUT counter-clockwise to the green, OFF (O) position. Wait 5 minutes for dissipation of stored energy. DANGER Fatal electric shock hazard Lethal voltages are present in the ISC (integrated system cabinet). Do a system shutdown, and then do LOTO on the main PDU breaker. The capacitors may have 800 volts.

Note Put a tank under the water filter when bring the filer out , as some water will fluid out. (For cleaning the water filter) Use a brush to clean the water filter in clean water. Note If you are using the old water filter (5812755) on your site, no need to clean the water filter. Please replace it to the new water filter (5847519).

title: Draining coolant from SBGD
body: Connect the one drain hose with manual hand pump, then connect to the component (SBGA/ SBPS). Place the other drain hose to the tank, then connect to the quick connector on the component (SBGA/SBPS). Pump the manual pump to remove the coolant. product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Draining coolant from ISR
body: Move the component (RFM / OM / MTD) out of the scan room. Warning Strong magnetic field The hand pump includes ferrous material, which can become a dangerous projectile in the presence of the magnetic field that the magnet produces. Do not drain the coolant in magnet room. Connect the one drain hose with manual hand pump, then connect to the component. Place the other drain hose to the tank, then connect to the quick connector on the component.

product_system: SIGNA™ Prime MAX / SIGNA™ Prime Elite 1.5T
title: Draining coolant from chiller tank
body: Unscrew the cap from the chiller tank. Prepare draining tank and draining hose with L connector. Insert L connector to the tank draining nipple. The valve inside will open automatically by connecting the mating connector and draining will start. When the coolant fills Tank almost full (about 4 minutes), remove the L connector and replace the Tank. Then, connect the L connector to nipple to restart the draining. Wait until the draining stops from the hose.

title: Starting up the host computer
body: Most service functionality, including software updates and patches, can be completed with operator-level privileges. body: If only a functional check is required, see Doing a B0 Drift functional check. If the functional check fails, see Running B0 Drift calibration. Unwanted changes in the main magnetic field strength can occur when the spatially uniform field component is altered for a short term, during the process of scanning, or when the spatially uniform field component is permanently altered. body: Place the TLT phantom on the table. Position the phantom in the center of the cradle and center it on the PA coil. To achieve the best test measurement, the phantom must be located in the center (long direction) of the cradle (landmark the center of phantom at 1080 mm from Home Position). Move the table in until it is 1080 mm from the home position. Adjust the phantom position and landmark on the crosshairs of the body TL loader at 1080 mm from home position.

title: Doing system gain calibration
body: System gain calibration determines the body and T/R (transmit/receive) head recon scale factors that will achieve a known level of image intensity when you use the body and T/R head coils with a known phantom solution and protocol. The goal is that when the same solution or tissue is scanned in the standard body and T/R head coils with the same protocol, those tissues will have approximately the same image intensity level on a given system and between systems of like type.

title: Doing the Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) check
body: The Multi-Coil Quality Assurance (MCQA) tool simplifies data acquisition and analysis of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) for surface coils. It helps detect dead coil elements and develop improved integrated signal-to-noise ratio (ISNR) specifications for all multi-coils independent of scanner instabilities. The ISNR measurement technique used is not dependent on coil or phantom geometry problems.

body: This section provides instructions for centering the phantom. There is no need to run a three-plane localizer before scanning because the tool automatically performs a phantom centering check. The tool also has a built-in wait time to allow the phantom to settle before scanning. The Probe Tuning and SNR Check Tool is an essential part of conditioning a system for performing spectroscopy, to optimize both SNR and phasing.

body: Go to the Service Desktop and select Calibrations from the Service Browser. Select DC Offset Calibration. Figure 1. DC Offset Calibration Select Run. A report of DC Offset calibration has been completed indicates that the calibration is done. You should only run the calibration one time. The calibration values are stored in /usr/g/caldir/gradient_tune.dat. Note The calibration values are relative to the site DC Offsets is run on and can vary greatly from site to site.

title: Running eddy current compensation
body: Eddy current compensation adjusts and compensates short, medium, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Use the following procedure to do eddy current compensation. Eddy current compensation should be run in Auto mode first. If Auto mode fails to bring any of the terms into specification, Manual mode can be used. Eddy current compensation uses dedicated pulse sequences, Head TLT/SWS phantom.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > Gradient
anchor: Eddy current compensation adjusts and compensates short, medium, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms.

doc_title: SIGNA™ Victor / SIGNA™ Star AIR / SIGNA™ Aviator AIR 1.5T General Service Manual
product_system: SIGNA™ Victor / SIGNA™ Star AIR / SIGNA™ Aviator AIR 1.5T
title: Running eddy current compensation in Manual mode
body: Select the Manual Mode tab. Figure 1. Manual Mode tab Select the desired terms and click Scan. If the Prompt to Accept mode is active, a graph of the results shows after the scan is completed. If a good fit is shown (fit line aligned with data line), click Accept. The calibration values are saved to disk and used in the next scan. Repeat this process by setting desired terms for the next scan and select Scan. If a bad fit is shown, click Cancel.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > Gradient > Running eddy current compensation
anchor: Select the Manual Mode tab.

title: Calibrating High Order Eddy Current (HOEC)
body: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order. This calibration works in conjunction with eddy current compensation, which adjusts and compensates the short, long, and very long time constant eddy currents for both linear and B0 terms. Run the HOEC calibration any time after eddy current compensation is done on the system.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations > Gradient
anchor: Use the High Order Eddy Current (HOEC) procedure to characterize the time dependent magnetic field errors in the bore up to at least the third order.

title: Doing power monitor function check (head and body)
body: The Power monitor functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power. It compares the measured RF power from the Power monitor to the expected value stored in the Power monitor configuration file. If two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the PM stops scanning.
section: Adjustments/Calibrations

title: Front and rear bridge leveling
body: Move cradle to end of rear bridge. Release cradle from LPCA and pull cradle back to home position. (For the LHFT) Lower patient table to lowest position. (For the FHFT) Install the caster wheels and move away. Measure the height difference between the rail surface of bridge and rear bridge. This difference should be less than ± 2 mm on each side. This can be done using the folding ruler (5897974). Note The folding ruler has a very small amount of ferrous content.

body: The Power monitor functional check runs a prescribed scan in the forward power. It compares the measured RF power from the Power monitor to the expected value stored in the Power monitor configuration file. If two values are outside 12%, the functional check fails. If the measured RF power exceeds the trip limit, the PM stops scanning.

body: Set up the Fluke ESA612 Safety Analyzer for testing. Turn on the safety analyzer. Select SETUP. Select F4 (More...). Select F2 (Instrument). Select F1 (Standard). Press ▲ (up arrow) until 60601 is visible. Select F4 (Done). Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F3 (Patient Auxiliary). The display shows polarity as OFF and neutral is blank, earth is closed. Press Polarity. The display shows polarity as Normal, neutral is closed, earth is closed.

body: Select μA to start the leakage test. Select F4 (More...). Select F1 (Select). On the display, Patient should be highlighted. The display shows polarity as Reverse, neutral is closed, earth is closed. Press ▼ (down arrow) to select DC Only. Press ► (right arrow) to select the lead connection to test. The lead under test will be highlighted. Measure all four leads and verify that the leakage current displayed on the meter is less than 50 microamps.

title: Arc Flash Safety
body: Arc flash is a high-energy discharge of highly-conductive plasma, which can cause destruction to anything in its path. It is important to take the proper precautions when servicing energized equipment where voltage exceeds 50 volts. All unguarded equipment being serviced posing immediate exposure to voltages greater than 50 volts requires appropriate Personnel Protective Equipment (PPE) be worn. Arc flash hazards are very complex and different than electrical shock hazards.

title: General Guidelines
body: Arc flash risks are recognized globally as a potential electrical hazard. Requirements and protective measures are guided by local regulatory requirements. In jurisdictions where PPE is specified, Hazard Class 1 or 2 PPE must be used. Arc flash may occur when de-energizing or re-energizing electrical equipment. Precautions must be taken during both actions. Comply with local regulatory requirements.

body: The system login control features are in the component Enterprise Authentication Authorization Audit (EA3). EA3 manages authentication and authorization on GE Healthcare Products. It supports local authentication and can also authenticate against Enterprise directory servers (MSAD, LDAP, and so on) to do enterprise authentication. title: Configuring password controls
body: Open the EA3 Administration window. Click the Local Users tab. Enter 3 in the Max Logon Attempts Before Lock field. The allowable range is 0-231. Enter 999999999 (or less, if indicated) in the Lock Duration (Minutes) field. Enter 8 (or greater, if indicated) in the Minimum Password Length field. The allowable range is 8-14. Select the Advanced Password Rules checkbox. Click Apply Configuration.
